title: Drift Harbor patch rollback runbook
brief: Quillfeather Interactive's Live Ops team needs a runbook for rolling back a bad game client patch on its online game Drift Harbor, owned by Live Ops, version 2026-10-13. Section "When to roll back": crash rate above 2 percent of sessions for 15 minutes, or login failures above 5 percent for 10 minutes, after a patch release; the Live Ops lead must approve in the #liveops-war-room channel. Section "Do not roll back if": the patch contained a database schema migration, such as migration 0087 in patch 4.13, in which case go forward with a hotfix instead because older clients cannot read the new schema. Section "Rollback steps" in order, with sub-steps. 1 Stop the bleeding: a) pause the deploy pipeline, b) set matchmaking to maintenance mode with the in-game message "Back soon". 2 Point players to the last good build: a) in the release console, set the live manifest to build 4.12.3, b) invalidate the CDN cache, which takes about 10 minutes. 3 Verify: a) install the build on 3 test accounts, one each on PC, console and mobile, b) confirm login and a full match. 4 Reopen in stages: a) let in 10 percent of players, b) 25 percent after 5 minutes, c) 50 percent after 5 more minutes, d) 100 percent after another 5 minutes if the crash rate stays under 1 percent. 5 Communicate: a) post a status update within 30 minutes of the decision, b) schedule compensation of 500 gems for every active account. Make sure readers do not miss that rolling back after a schema migration corrupts player inventories. Add a final section "Contacts": Live Ops lead, Soledad Ortega; Release engineer on call, Thabo Mokoena; Community manager, Ji-ho Han.

edit.request: Change the crash-rate trigger from 2 percent to 3 percent, and add a sub-step to step 5: "Update the public status page".
